news.body:
## What moved
- You cleared the Campus France file and two of the career platforms.
The EEF was validated and the fee paid on 6 October, the extra documents went on the 5th, and VMock access and Case Coach were both closed the same day. Five tasks closed in the week, all of them yours rather than anyone else's.
- The visa turned out to be three weeks earlier than the board thought.
Campus France refused the interview exemption on Thursday, which revived a task you had deleted, and in the same conversation Fitria put submission at about two working days after the interview. That moved it from 10 November to 23 October, and the provider is TLS Contact, not VFS.
- On Saturday evening you did the unglamorous half.
The France-Visas account, your employer's details for the form, and a request to SBI for an in-principle sanction letter. None of it shows as a tick and all three were holding up the submission.

## What did not
- The SBI branch has not written since 6 October.
Their last substantive word was on 27 September, that verification of the collateral would take more time. Two requests are sitting with them now, not one.
- Your degree originals are still with the courier.
Wednesday's interview needs them in your hand, and nothing on the board says where the parcel is.
- Career did not move at all.
Writing down your post-MBA function, industry and geography is still open, and CareerGlobe, the two questionnaires, the CV and the first CDC session all sit behind it.

## Risks
- The passport window is the one that can cost you the flight.
TLS keeps your passport from submission until the decision, about fifteen days by Fitria's account. Submitting on 16 October gets it back near the end of the month; submitting on the 23rd gets it back around 7 November, the day you leave Jakarta, and you need it for the KITAS exit permit as well. Every day between the interview and the submission comes off that margin.
- Proof of funds has quietly become a visa problem and not only a tuition one.
The loan used to be a 5 November deadline. The visa file now needs evidence of it too, and both requests sit with the same branch that has gone quiet. If the in-principle letter does not come, the submission has nothing to show.
- One parcel gates the whole visa sequence.
The interview, the submission, the decision and the exit permit all run off a courier nobody has a tracking number for.
- The career chain is the cheapest thing to fix and the most expensive to leave.
One question only you can answer unblocks four tasks, and the first CDC coaching session is already dated 15 November.

## Put first this week
- Write back to Fitria and confirm Wednesday. One line, and everything downstream waits on it.
- Call the branch on Monday, and ask for the in-principle letter and the state of the full sanction in the same call.
- Get the tracking number today, so Tuesday is not when you find out the parcel is late.
- Answer the post-MBA question. Nobody outside is holding that one up.
